devdoc.details: ------------------------------------------------------------------      WHAT CHANGED FROM #6, AND NOTHING ELSE DID      ------------------------------------------------------------------      A copy of {ArgusV4LaunchToken6}, Portal #6's deployed `tokenImpl`, which      is not edited. Three changes (SPEC_PORTAL7.md §2.1):        1. {initialize} takes a TENTH argument, `payoutAsset_`, and a           `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker pays in THAT rather than in the ninth,           `quoteAsset_`. Portal #7 passes the pool quote when the quote is           keep-listed and USDC when it is not (SPEC_QUOTE_AUTO_ADMISSION.md           §5b). {quoteAsset} still stores the ninth argument, so it still           answers what the pool is paired against. That is the whole reason           this contract exists instead of reusing #6's token with USDC as its           ninth argument (qa-11 §2.3, option ii, the owner's ruling).        2. `payoutAsset_` must be `quoteAsset_` or {defaultQuoteAsset}, and is           refused otherwise ({PayoutAssetNotAllowed}). Those are the only two           values Portal #7 passes, and a tracker paying a third asset could           not be funded by the splitter, which pays holders only in the quote,           in USDC, or in the token.        3. `extraExempt` is `memory`, for the stack. See {initialize}.      THE TRACKER IS UNCHANGED. The constructor creates the same      {ArgusV4RewardTracker6} Portal #6's token creates. Its {receive} accepts      native only when its payout asset is Arc USDC, which under Portal #7 is      true of every non-keep QUOTE launch as well as of every USDC one.      THE TESTS NAMED BELOW RUN AGAINST THE ORIGINALS. Every `test_*` cited in      the text carried over from #6 and #5 was written against those contracts.      What executes against THIS contract is      `test/unit/ArgusV4LaunchToken7.t.sol`, which ports #6's nineteen and adds      the payout-argument cases and the no-mint and no-owner-power guarantees.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      #6's HEADER, CARRIED OVER      ------------------------------------------------------------------      {ArgusV4LaunchToken} WITH THE QUOTE MOVED FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION TO THE      CLONE. That contract is Portal #5's deployed `tokenImpl` and is not      edited; this is a copy (SPEC_PORTAL6.md §2.5). The original holds      `quoteAsset` as an IMMUTABLE, so every clone reads one value, and its      `_wireRewards` makes that value the payout asset of every      `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker. Behind a Portal that admits a quote per      launch, that is a dividend paid in USDC by a launch that only ever      collects its own quote. Four changes, and nothing else differs:        1. The immutable stays, renamed {defaultQuoteAsset}: the quote this           implementation was built for, and the one value a Portal can check           at deploy. NOTHING in this contract reads it after the constructor.        2. {initialize} takes a NINTH argument, `quoteAsset_`, stored per clone           as {quoteAsset} and handed to {_wireRewards}. A QUOTE tracker pays           in THAT. The selector moves from `0xc4ee371e` to `0x92e481f4`,           fixed by {IArgusV4LaunchToken6}, which this contract inherits.        3. The tracker implementation is CREATED by the constructor, not passed           in. {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-initialize} has the same selector as the           original tracker's, so a deploy that handed this token the OLD           tracker would compile, deploy and launch, and the only symptom would           be native stranded in a non-USDC QUOTE tracker. With no argument           there is nothing to hand it. Read the address from {trackerImpl}.        4. The tracker is {ArgusV4RewardTracker6}, whose {receive} accepts           native only when the payout asset is Arc USDC.      The exemption set is unchanged and is written exactly as before.      THE TESTS NAMED BELOW RUN AGAINST THE ORIGINAL. Every `test_*` cited in      the text carried over from {ArgusV4LaunchToken} was written against that      contract and still executes against it. They describe this code because      it is that code outside the four changes; they do not execute it. What      executes against THIS contract is `test/unit/ArgusV4LaunchToken6.t.sol`.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      THE THREE BINDING REQUIREMENTS, QUOTED AND SATISFIED      ------------------------------------------------------------------      `ArgusV4Portal`'s note on {IArgusV4LaunchToken} states them:        "THREE binding requirements on any `tokenImpl` follow, and the third is         easy to miss: it must mint EXACTLY `totalSupply` and no more, in         `initialize`; it must not inflate during the mint; and IT MUST NOT         TREAT `0x...dEaD` AS A BURN ADDRESS"      R1 - MINT EXACTLY `totalSupply`, IN `initialize`. {initialize} calls      `_mint(supplyRecipient, totalSupply_)` exactly once and there is no other      `_mint` in this contract. Pinned by `test_R1_exactSupplyIsMinted`.      R2 - DO NOT INFLATE DURING THE MINT. {_update} moves balances and calls      the tracker; it never mints, and this contract has NO mint entry point of      any kind - not owner-gated, not portal-gated, none. Pinned by      `test_R2_totalSupplyIsConstantAcrossTheWholeLaunch`, which reads      `totalSupply()` before and after a real Portal launch.      R3 - `0x...dEaD` IS AN ORDINARY HOLDER. It is deliberately NOT special      anywhere in this file: no burn-on-transfer, no `_burn`, no exclusion from      `totalSupply()`. `ArgusV4Portal._mintCurve` transfers the rounding residue      there BEFORE reading the anchor, so a token that      burned on transfer to that address would fail `SupplyNotAnchored` on EVERY      launch - the Portal measured the largest residue at 254,169,568 wei out of      1e27. Pinned by `test_R3_deadIsAnOrdinaryHolder`.      🔴 AND THE ANCHOR IS A CONSISTENCY CHECK, NOT AN HONESTY CHECK, SO THE      REQUIREMENTS ABOVE ARE NOT WHAT MAKES THIS TOKEN SAFE. The same note is      explicit that a `tokenImpl` reporting the asked-for supply while      crediting ten times that to the creator launches cleanly, and that an      implementation with a mint entry point can dilute the curve in the SAME      transaction. Those are properties of the implementation and this is the      implementation, so they are answered here rather than by the Portal:      exactly one `_mint`, to exactly the address the Portal names, and no      second credit to anybody. `test_H1_noHiddenPremint` and      `test_H2_noMintEntryPointExists` are the two that hold it.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      NO TRANSFER TAX, AND IT IS NOT A PREFERENCE      ------------------------------------------------------------------      A transfer-based tax cannot survive Uniswap v4. A trader may take swap      proceeds as an ERC-6909 CLAIM against the PoolManager, in which case no      ERC-20 `transfer` of this token happens at all, {_update} never runs, and      a tax jar stays empty. Re-measured for this contract at the pin in      `V4_LAUNCH_TOKEN_REPORT.md` §2, with a positive control in the same run:      the identical token taxes an ERC-20-settled swap and does not tax a      claim-settled one, so the instrument can detect a tax and the absence is      a finding rather than a silence.      So the tax is not implemented, disabled or left at zero - it is ABSENT,      and the reward stream is funded from outside this contract instead. See      {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-deposit} and §5 of the report.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      IMMUTABLES HERE, AND WHY THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF `ArgusTaxToken`      ------------------------------------------------------------------      `ArgusTaxToken`'s header says "Nothing here is `immutable`" because an      immutable lives in the IMPLEMENTATION's runtime code, so every clone reads      the implementation's value - the same tax rate, the same creator wallet,      on every launch. That reasoning is correct and it is about PER-LAUNCH      config. The four immutables below are per-DEPLOYMENT constants: the same      tracker implementation, the same PoolManager, the same DEFAULT quote and      the same config registry for every launch this pad will ever do. For      those, a clone reading the implementation's value is exactly the wanted      behaviour and it saves cold SLOADs on every launch.      THE LAUNCH'S QUOTE IS NO LONGER ONE OF THEM, and that is `ArgusTaxToken`'s      reasoning applied rather than overturned: once a Portal admits a quote per      launch, the quote is per-launch config, and per-launch config lives in      storage. On the original it was an immutable because its Portal could only      ever name one.      That a clone really does read the four is not assumed:      `test_C1_aCloneReadsTheImplementationsImmutables` asserts it.      Everything that varies per launch - name, symbol, supply, owner, reward      mode, quote - is in storage, written once by {initialize}.

constructor.details: Locks the implementation. A clone gets fresh storage and initializes      normally; the implementation can never be initialized, so nobody can      take ownership of the address every clone points at. `ArgusV4Portal`      depends on this - `_deployParts` clones and initializes in one      transaction precisely because an un-run `initialize` is claimable.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

initialize(string,string,string,uint256,.details: THE SIGNATURE IS FIXED BY {IArgusV4LaunchToken7}, which this contract      inherits, so a drift is a compile error. `test_S1` in      `ArgusV4LaunchToken7.t.sol` also asserts the literal, so changing the      interface and this function together is still a red test.      `quoteAsset_` is the ninth argument, as on #6: the asset the Portal      admitted this launch under and paired its pool against. Stored as      {quoteAsset} and read by nothing on the payout path. Zero is refused.      `payoutAsset_` is the tenth and the only new one: what a      `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker pays holders in. It must be `quoteAsset_`      (a keep-listed quote, or the default) or {defaultQuoteAsset} (USDC,      for a quote that is converted). Anything else, zero included, is      {PayoutAssetNotAllowed}. Checked under every mode, so a Portal that      passes a wrong value fails on its first launch rather than on its      first QUOTE-mode launch.      The three strings are `memory` where the original's are `calldata`,      and that is the stack rather than a preference: nine arguments with      three calldata strings and a calldata array are one slot too deep for      the legacy code generator INSIDE THE ABI DECODER (`forge build`:      "Stack too deep ... dataEnd"), and `via_ir` is not this repository's      setting. A `memory` string is one stack slot, a `calldata` one is two.      The TENTH argument is paid for the same way: `extraExempt` moves to      `memory` as well, which is one more slot freed. Data location is not      part of the ABI, so the selector does not depend on it.      `extraExempt` carries the fee locker on a Portal launch, and the      Portal's note says why it is the one address a v4 launch must exempt:      "the locker receives the token side of the LP fees straight out of the      PoolManager, which a tax token would read as a buy"      (`ArgusV4Portal`'s note on {IArgusV4LaunchToken}). This token has no tax, so there is      no buy to misread - but the locker must still be out of the reward      denominator, because it is handed the token side of every fee harvest      and would otherwise accrue rewards on value it is about to burn. The      list is passed straight through to the tracker.

logo().details: THE NAME IS THE FEATURE, exactly as in `ArgusTaxToken`: `logo()` is      selector `0xfb7f21eb` and it is the first thing explorers, wallets and      this repository's own `tools/arc-tokens.mjs` staticcall for a token's      art. A token that only emits its image in a launch event is invisible      to all of them.

name().details: ERC20's `_name`/`_symbol` are written by ITS constructor, which never      runs for a clone - a clone would report the implementation's empty      strings. These read our own storage instead.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

totalSupply().details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

SHARE_SYNC_GAS.details: Gas ceiling on each {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}.      LOWER THAN {ArgusTaxToken-SHARE_SYNC_GAS}'s 200,000 ON PURPOSE, and      the reason is P-3 of the tracker: the ~113k path where the v3 tracker      first LEARNS the pool address and un-counts a share it had already      credited does not exist here, because the excluded venue is passed in      at initialize and there is no lazy discovery on the transfer path.      What remains is the early-out (~2.5k), the ordinary update, and a      first-time holder's three cold SSTOREs plus the one-off      `totalSupply()` staticcall.      Undersizing this is SILENT and permanent: the try/catch swallows the      out-of-gas, the transfer succeeds, and that holder's share is never      recorded. `test_G1_shareSyncGasClearsTheMeasuredWorstCase` measures      the real worst case and asserts this constant clears it, so the      number is checked against the code rather than against a comment.

defaultQuoteAsset.details: NOT what a launch pays rewards in - that is {quoteAsset}, per clone.      Kept for one reader: a Portal cross-checks it against its own default      at deploy, so a `tokenImpl` built for a different default is refused      before any launch. Nothing in this contract reads it after the      constructor.

isExempt.details: Mirrors what the tracker was initialized with. Fixed forever: there      is deliberately no setter, so an exemption can never be handed out or      revoked after launch. Same discipline as      `ArgusTaxToken`'s `isExempt`.

launchConfig.details: Read ONCE, during {initialize}, keyed by `owner` - which      the Portal's `_deployParts` sets to its own `msg.sender`, so the key is      the creator that signed the launch. See {ArgusV4LaunchConfig} for why the config cannot ride      the seam.

owner.details: 🔴 A LABEL, NOT A ROLE. Nothing in this contract is gated on it:      there is no `onlyOwner`, no `reduceTaxes` (there are no taxes), no      `renounce` (there is nothing to renounce) and no mint. It is stored      for two uses and no others - it is the key {_wireRewards} reads the      creator's config under, and it is what explorers and this pad's front      end display. `test_H3_ownerHasNoPowers` enumerates every      state-changing entry point and asserts none of them consults it after      {initialize}.

poolManager.details: 🔴 THE EXCLUSION IS UNAVOIDABLY BROADER THAN "THE POOL", AND THAT IS      THE ONE COST OF REWARDS ON v4. Under v3 the pool is a contract with      its own address and excluding it excludes exactly the pool's      inventory. Under v4 there is no pool contract: this ONE address holds      every pool's inventory on the chain AND every ERC-20-6909 claim      balance any user has chosen to leave inside the PoolManager. So      excluding it also excludes a real holder who holds a claim rather than      the token.      The behaviour is disclosed rather than worked around, and the      workaround is a holder's to take: REDEEM THE CLAIM INTO THE ORDINARY      TOKEN AND THE SHARE APPEARS. Redemption is an ERC-20 transfer out of      the PoolManager, so it runs {_update} and {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}      like any other receipt. Constructed and then restored in      `test_X1_aClaimHolderIsExcluded` / `test_X2_redemptionRestoresTheShare`,      and §4 of the report gives the measured cost.

quoteAsset.details: NOT NECESSARILY WHAT A `RewardMode.QUOTE` TRACKER PAYS IN, and that      is change 1. Under Portal #7 a non-keep quote's tracker pays USDC;      read the tracker's own `payoutAsset()` for the payout. This getter      keeps answering the pairing, which is what "paired against" means to      every reader that already calls it.      Per clone, written once by {initialize}, never zero on a clone.      `address(0)` on the IMPLEMENTATION, and that is deliberate: a Portal      that still reads `quoteAsset()` off the implementation for its      deploy-time check gets zero and refuses, loudly, rather than accepting      a token whose quote it has misread. Such a Portal must read      {defaultQuoteAsset}. NOTHING here assumes its decimals; see the      tracker's P-2.

trackerImpl.details: Created by the constructor, never passed in - change 3 in the contract      note. A contract-created address, so it is not a top-level deployment:      a verifier or a deploy script reads it from here.

logo().details: THE NAME IS THE FEATURE, exactly as in `ArgusTaxToken`: `logo()` is      selector `0xfb7f21eb` and it is the first thing explorers, wallets and      this repository's own `tools/arc-tokens.mjs` staticcall for a token's      art. name().details: ERC20's `_name`/`_symbol` are written by ITS constructor, which never      runs for a clone - a clone would report the implementation's empty      strings. These read our own storage instead.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

constructor.details: Locks the implementation. A clone gets fresh storage and initializes      normally; the implementation can never be initialized, so nobody can      take ownership of the address every clone points at. `ArgusV4Portal`      depends on this - `_deployParts` clones and initializes in one      transaction precisely because an un-run `initialize` is claimable.

totalSupply().details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.

balanceOf(address).details: Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

owner.details: 🔴 A LABEL, NOT A ROLE. Nothing in this contract is gated on it:      there is no `onlyOwner`, no `reduceTaxes` (there are no taxes), no      `renounce` (there is nothing to renounce) and no mint. It is stored      for two uses and no others - it is the key {_wireRewards} reads the      creator's config under, and it is what explorers and this pad's front      end display. `test_H3_ownerHasNoPowers` enumerates every      state-changing entry point and asserts none of them consults it after      {initialize}.

isExempt.details: Mirrors what the tracker was initialized with. Fixed forever: there      is deliberately no setter, so an exemption can never be handed out or      revoked after launch. Same discipline as      `ArgusTaxToken`'s `isExempt`.

quoteAsset.details: NOT NECESSARILY WHAT A `RewardMode.QUOTE` TRACKER PAYS IN, and that      is change 1. Under Portal #7 a non-keep quote's tracker pays USDC;      read the tracker's own `payoutAsset()` for the payout. This getter      keeps answering the pairing, which is what "paired against" means to      every reader that already calls it.      Per clone, written once by {initialize}, never zero on a clone.      `address(0)` on the IMPLEMENTATION, and that is deliberate: a Portal      that still reads `quoteAsset()` off the implementation for its      deploy-time check gets zero and refuses, loudly, rather than accepting      a token whose quote it has misread. Such a Portal must read      {defaultQuoteAsset}. NOTHING here assumes its decimals; see the      tracker's P-2.

poolManager.details: 🔴 THE EXCLUSION IS UNAVOIDABLY BROADER THAN "THE POOL", AND THAT IS      THE ONE COST OF REWARDS ON v4. Under v3 the pool is a contract with      its own address and excluding it excludes exactly the pool's      inventory. Under v4 there is no pool contract: this ONE address holds      every pool's inventory on the chain AND every ERC-20-6909 claim      balance any user has chosen to leave inside the PoolManager. So      excluding it also excludes a real holder who holds a claim rather than      the token.      The behaviour is disclosed rather than worked around, and the      workaround is a holder's to take: REDEEM THE CLAIM INTO THE ORDINARY      TOKEN AND THE SHARE APPEARS. Redemption is an ERC-20 transfer out of      the PoolManager, so it runs {_update} and {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}      like any other receipt. Constructed and then restored in      `test_X1_aClaimHolderIsExcluded` / `test_X2_redemptionRestoresTheShare`,      and §4 of the report gives the measured cost.

trackerImpl.details: Created by the constructor, never passed in - change 3 in the contract      note. A contract-created address, so it is not a top-level deployment:      a verifier or a deploy script reads it from here.

launchConfig.details: Read ONCE, during {initialize}, keyed by `owner` - which      the Portal's `_deployParts` sets to its own `msg.sender`, so the key is      the creator that signed the launch. See {ArgusV4LaunchConfig} for why the config cannot ride      the seam.

SHARE_SYNC_GAS.details: Gas ceiling on each {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}.      LOWER THAN {ArgusTaxToken-SHARE_SYNC_GAS}'s 200,000 ON PURPOSE, and      the reason is P-3 of the tracker: the ~113k path where the v3 tracker      first LEARNS the pool address and un-counts a share it had already      credited does not exist here, because the excluded venue is passed in      at initialize and there is no lazy discovery on the transfer path.      What remains is the early-out (~2.5k), the ordinary update, and a      first-time holder's three cold SSTOREs plus the one-off      `totalSupply()` staticcall.      Undersizing this is SILENT and permanent: the try/catch swallows the      out-of-gas, the transfer succeeds, and that holder's share is never      recorded. `test_G1_shareSyncGasClearsTheMeasuredWorstCase` measures      the real worst case and asserts this constant clears it, so the      number is checked against the code rather than against a comment.

defaultQuoteAsset.details: NOT what a launch pays rewards in - that is {quoteAsset}, per clone.      Kept for one reader: a Portal cross-checks it against its own default      at deploy, so a `tokenImpl` built for a different default is refused      before any launch. Nothing in this contract reads it after the      constructor.

devdoc.details: ------------------------------------------------------------------      WHAT CHANGED FROM #6, AND NOTHING ELSE DID      ------------------------------------------------------------------      A copy of {ArgusV4LaunchToken6}, Portal #6's deployed `tokenImpl`, which      is not edited. Three changes (SPEC_PORTAL7.md §2.1):        1. {initialize} takes a TENTH argument, `payoutAsset_`, and a           `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker pays in THAT rather than in the ninth,           `quoteAsset_`. Portal #7 passes the pool quote when the quote is           keep-listed and USDC when it is not (SPEC_QUOTE_AUTO_ADMISSION.md           §5b). {quoteAsset} still stores the ninth argument, so it still           answers what the pool is paired against. That is the whole reason           this contract exists instead of reusing #6's token with USDC as its           ninth argument (qa-11 §2.3, option ii, the owner's ruling).        2. `payoutAsset_` must be `quoteAsset_` or {defaultQuoteAsset}, and is           refused otherwise ({PayoutAssetNotAllowed}). Those are the only two           values Portal #7 passes, and a tracker paying a third asset could           not be funded by the splitter, which pays holders only in the quote,           in USDC, or in the token.        3. `extraExempt` is `memory`, for the stack. See {initialize}.      THE TRACKER IS UNCHANGED. The constructor creates the same      {ArgusV4RewardTracker6} Portal #6's token creates. Its {receive} accepts      native only when its payout asset is Arc USDC, which under Portal #7 is      true of every non-keep QUOTE launch as well as of every USDC one.      THE TESTS NAMED BELOW RUN AGAINST THE ORIGINALS. Every `test_*` cited in      the text carried over from #6 and #5 was written against those contracts.      What executes against THIS contract is      `test/unit/ArgusV4LaunchToken7.t.sol`, which ports #6's nineteen and adds      the payout-argument cases and the no-mint and no-owner-power guarantees.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      #6's HEADER, CARRIED OVER      ------------------------------------------------------------------      {ArgusV4LaunchToken} WITH THE QUOTE MOVED FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION TO THE      CLONE. That contract is Portal #5's deployed `tokenImpl` and is not      edited; this is a copy (SPEC_PORTAL6.md §2.5). The original holds      `quoteAsset` as an IMMUTABLE, so every clone reads one value, and its      `_wireRewards` makes that value the payout asset of every      `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker. Behind a Portal that admits a quote per      launch, that is a dividend paid in USDC by a launch that only ever      collects its own quote. Four changes, and nothing else differs:        1. The immutable stays, renamed {defaultQuoteAsset}: the quote this           implementation was built for, and the one value a Portal can check           at deploy. NOTHING in this contract reads it after the constructor.        2. {initialize} takes a NINTH argument, `quoteAsset_`, stored per clone           as {quoteAsset} and handed to {_wireRewards}. A QUOTE tracker pays           in THAT. The selector moves from `0xc4ee371e` to `0x92e481f4`,           fixed by {IArgusV4LaunchToken6}, which this contract inherits.        3. The tracker implementation is CREATED by the constructor, not passed           in. {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-initialize} has the same selector as the           original tracker's, so a deploy that handed this token the OLD           tracker would compile, deploy and launch, and the only symptom would           be native stranded in a non-USDC QUOTE tracker. With no argument           there is nothing to hand it. Read the address from {trackerImpl}.        4. The tracker is {ArgusV4RewardTracker6}, whose {receive} accepts           native only when the payout asset is Arc USDC.      The exemption set is unchanged and is written exactly as before.      THE TESTS NAMED BELOW RUN AGAINST THE ORIGINAL. Every `test_*` cited in      the text carried over from {ArgusV4LaunchToken} was written against that      contract and still executes against it. They describe this code because      it is that code outside the four changes; they do not execute it. What      executes against THIS contract is `test/unit/ArgusV4LaunchToken6.t.sol`.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      THE THREE BINDING REQUIREMENTS, QUOTED AND SATISFIED      ------------------------------------------------------------------      `ArgusV4Portal`'s note on {IArgusV4LaunchToken} states them:        "THREE binding requirements on any `tokenImpl` follow, and the third is         easy to miss: it must mint EXACTLY `totalSupply` and no more, in         `initialize`; it must not inflate during the mint; and IT MUST NOT         TREAT `0x...dEaD` AS A BURN ADDRESS"      R1 - MINT EXACTLY `totalSupply`, IN `initialize`. {initialize} calls      `_mint(supplyRecipient, totalSupply_)` exactly once and there is no other      `_mint` in this contract. Pinned by `test_R1_exactSupplyIsMinted`.      R2 - DO NOT INFLATE DURING THE MINT. {_update} moves balances and calls      the tracker; it never mints, and this contract has NO mint entry point of      any kind - not owner-gated, not portal-gated, none. Pinned by      `test_R2_totalSupplyIsConstantAcrossTheWholeLaunch`, which reads      `totalSupply()` before and after a real Portal launch.      R3 - `0x...dEaD` IS AN ORDINARY HOLDER. It is deliberately NOT special      anywhere in this file: no burn-on-transfer, no `_burn`, no exclusion from      `totalSupply()`. `ArgusV4Portal._mintCurve` transfers the rounding residue      there BEFORE reading the anchor, so a token that      burned on transfer to that address would fail `SupplyNotAnchored` on EVERY      launch - the Portal measured the largest residue at 254,169,568 wei out of      1e27. Pinned by `test_R3_deadIsAnOrdinaryHolder`.      🔴 AND THE ANCHOR IS A CONSISTENCY CHECK, NOT AN HONESTY CHECK, SO THE      REQUIREMENTS ABOVE ARE NOT WHAT MAKES THIS TOKEN SAFE. The same note is      explicit that a `tokenImpl` reporting the asked-for supply while      crediting ten times that to the creator launches cleanly, and that an      implementation with a mint entry point can dilute the curve in the SAME      transaction. Those are properties of the implementation and this is the      implementation, so they are answered here rather than by the Portal:      exactly one `_mint`, to exactly the address the Portal names, and no      second credit to anybody. `test_H1_noHiddenPremint` and      `test_H2_noMintEntryPointExists` are the two that hold it.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      NO TRANSFER TAX, AND IT IS NOT A PREFERENCE      ------------------------------------------------------------------      A transfer-based tax cannot survive Uniswap v4. A trader may take swap      proceeds as an ERC-6909 CLAIM against the PoolManager, in which case no      ERC-20 `transfer` of this token happens at all, {_update} never runs, and      a tax jar stays empty. Re-measured for this contract at the pin in      `V4_LAUNCH_TOKEN_REPORT.md` §2, with a positive control in the same run:      the identical token taxes an ERC-20-settled swap and does not tax a      claim-settled one, so the instrument can detect a tax and the absence is      a finding rather than a silence.      So the tax is not implemented, disabled or left at zero - it is ABSENT,      and the reward stream is funded from outside this contract instead. See      {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-deposit} and §5 of the report.      ------------------------------------------------------------------      IMMUTABLES HERE, AND WHY THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF `ArgusTaxToken`      ------------------------------------------------------------------      `ArgusTaxToken`'s header says "Nothing here is `immutable`" because an      immutable lives in the IMPLEMENTATION's runtime code, so every clone reads      the implementation's value - the same tax rate, the same creator wallet,      on every launch. That reasoning is correct and it is about PER-LAUNCH      config. The four immutables below are per-DEPLOYMENT constants: the same      tracker implementation, the same PoolManager, the same DEFAULT quote and      the same config registry for every launch this pad will ever do. For      those, a clone reading the implementation's value is exactly the wanted      behaviour and it saves cold SLOADs on every launch.      THE LAUNCH'S QUOTE IS NO LONGER ONE OF THEM, and that is `ArgusTaxToken`'s      reasoning applied rather than overturned: once a Portal admits a quote per      launch, the quote is per-launch config, and per-launch config lives in      storage. On the original it was an immutable because its Portal could only      ever name one.      That a clone really does read the four is not assumed:      `test_C1_aCloneReadsTheImplementationsImmutables` asserts it.      Everything that varies per launch - name, symbol, supply, owner, reward      mode, quote - is in storage, written once by {initialize}.

logo().details: THE NAME IS THE FEATURE, exactly as in `ArgusTaxToken`: `logo()` is      selector `0xfb7f21eb` and it is the first thing explorers, wallets and      this repository's own `tools/arc-tokens.mjs` staticcall for a token's      art. A token that only emits its image in a launch event is invisible      to all of them.

name().details: ERC20's `_name`/`_symbol` are written by ITS constructor, which never      runs for a clone - a clone would report the implementation's empty      strings. These read our own storage instead.

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

constructor.details: Locks the implementation. A clone gets fresh storage and initializes      normally; the implementation can never be initialized, so nobody can      take ownership of the address every clone points at. `ArgusV4Portal`      depends on this - `_deployParts` clones and initializes in one      transaction precisely because an un-run `initialize` is claimable.

totalSupply().details: Returns the value of tokens in existence.

balanceOf(address).details: Returns the value of tokens owned by `account`.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `value` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `value`.

allowance(address,address).details: Returns the remaining number of tokens that `spender` will be allowed to spend on behalf of `owner` through {transferFrom}. This is zero by default. This value changes when {approve} or {transferFrom} are called.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Skips emitting an {Approval} event indicating an allowance update. This is not required by the ERC. See {xref-ERC20-_approve-address-address-uint256-bool-}[_approve]. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `value`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `value`.

initialize(string,string,string,uint256,.details: THE SIGNATURE IS FIXED BY {IArgusV4LaunchToken7}, which this contract      inherits, so a drift is a compile error. `test_S1` in      `ArgusV4LaunchToken7.t.sol` also asserts the literal, so changing the      interface and this function together is still a red test.      `quoteAsset_` is the ninth argument, as on #6: the asset the Portal      admitted this launch under and paired its pool against. Stored as      {quoteAsset} and read by nothing on the payout path. Zero is refused.      `payoutAsset_` is the tenth and the only new one: what a      `RewardMode.QUOTE` tracker pays holders in. It must be `quoteAsset_`      (a keep-listed quote, or the default) or {defaultQuoteAsset} (USDC,      for a quote that is converted). Anything else, zero included, is      {PayoutAssetNotAllowed}. Checked under every mode, so a Portal that      passes a wrong value fails on its first launch rather than on its      first QUOTE-mode launch.      The three strings are `memory` where the original's are `calldata`,      and that is the stack rather than a preference: nine arguments with      three calldata strings and a calldata array are one slot too deep for      the legacy code generator INSIDE THE ABI DECODER (`forge build`:      "Stack too deep ... dataEnd"), and `via_ir` is not this repository's      setting. A `memory` string is one stack slot, a `calldata` one is two.      The TENTH argument is paid for the same way: `extraExempt` moves to      `memory` as well, which is one more slot freed. Data location is not      part of the ABI, so the selector does not depend on it.      `extraExempt` carries the fee locker on a Portal launch, and the      Portal's note says why it is the one address a v4 launch must exempt:      "the locker receives the token side of the LP fees straight out of the      PoolManager, which a tax token would read as a buy"      (`ArgusV4Portal`'s note on {IArgusV4LaunchToken}). This token has no tax, so there is      no buy to misread - but the locker must still be out of the reward      denominator, because it is handed the token side of every fee harvest      and would otherwise accrue rewards on value it is about to burn. The      list is passed straight through to the tracker.

owner.details: 🔴 A LABEL, NOT A ROLE. Nothing in this contract is gated on it:      there is no `onlyOwner`, no `reduceTaxes` (there are no taxes), no      `renounce` (there is nothing to renounce) and no mint. It is stored      for two uses and no others - it is the key {_wireRewards} reads the      creator's config under, and it is what explorers and this pad's front      end display. `test_H3_ownerHasNoPowers` enumerates every      state-changing entry point and asserts none of them consults it after      {initialize}.

isExempt.details: Mirrors what the tracker was initialized with. Fixed forever: there      is deliberately no setter, so an exemption can never be handed out or      revoked after launch. Same discipline as      `ArgusTaxToken`'s `isExempt`.

quoteAsset.details: NOT NECESSARILY WHAT A `RewardMode.QUOTE` TRACKER PAYS IN, and that      is change 1. Under Portal #7 a non-keep quote's tracker pays USDC;      read the tracker's own `payoutAsset()` for the payout. This getter      keeps answering the pairing, which is what "paired against" means to      every reader that already calls it.      Per clone, written once by {initialize}, never zero on a clone.      `address(0)` on the IMPLEMENTATION, and that is deliberate: a Portal      that still reads `quoteAsset()` off the implementation for its      deploy-time check gets zero and refuses, loudly, rather than accepting      a token whose quote it has misread. Such a Portal must read      {defaultQuoteAsset}. NOTHING here assumes its decimals; see the      tracker's P-2.

poolManager.details: 🔴 THE EXCLUSION IS UNAVOIDABLY BROADER THAN "THE POOL", AND THAT IS      THE ONE COST OF REWARDS ON v4. Under v3 the pool is a contract with      its own address and excluding it excludes exactly the pool's      inventory. Under v4 there is no pool contract: this ONE address holds      every pool's inventory on the chain AND every ERC-20-6909 claim      balance any user has chosen to leave inside the PoolManager. So      excluding it also excludes a real holder who holds a claim rather than      the token.      The behaviour is disclosed rather than worked around, and the      workaround is a holder's to take: REDEEM THE CLAIM INTO THE ORDINARY      TOKEN AND THE SHARE APPEARS. Redemption is an ERC-20 transfer out of      the PoolManager, so it runs {_update} and {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}      like any other receipt. Constructed and then restored in      `test_X1_aClaimHolderIsExcluded` / `test_X2_redemptionRestoresTheShare`,      and §4 of the report gives the measured cost.

trackerImpl.details: Created by the constructor, never passed in - change 3 in the contract      note. A contract-created address, so it is not a top-level deployment:      a verifier or a deploy script reads it from here.

launchConfig.details: Read ONCE, during {initialize}, keyed by `owner` - which      the Portal's `_deployParts` sets to its own `msg.sender`, so the key is      the creator that signed the launch. See {ArgusV4LaunchConfig} for why the config cannot ride      the seam.

SHARE_SYNC_GAS.details: Gas ceiling on each {ArgusV4RewardTracker6-setShare}.      LOWER THAN {ArgusTaxToken-SHARE_SYNC_GAS}'s 200,000 ON PURPOSE, and      the reason is P-3 of the tracker: the ~113k path where the v3 tracker      first LEARNS the pool address and un-counts a share it had already      credited does not exist here, because the excluded venue is passed in      at initialize and there is no lazy discovery on the transfer path.      What remains is the early-out (~2.5k), the ordinary update, and a      first-time holder's three cold SSTOREs plus the one-off      `totalSupply()` staticcall.      Undersizing this is SILENT and permanent: the try/catch swallows the      out-of-gas, the transfer succeeds, and that holder's share is never      recorded. `test_G1_shareSyncGasClearsTheMeasuredWorstCase` measures      the real worst case and asserts this constant clears it, so the      number is checked against the code rather than against a comment.

defaultQuoteAsset.details: NOT what a launch pays rewards in - that is {quoteAsset}, per clone.      Kept for one reader: a Portal cross-checks it against its own default      at deploy, so a `tokenImpl` built for a different default is refused      before any launch. Nothing in this contract reads it after the      constructor.
